title: Hosted API — Sentinel Forecast and Burst Planning (2028Q1)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines the sentinel-style peak load forecast for Hosted API for 2028 Q1, with explicit burst buckets, regional token/QPS projections, and headroom targets tied to GPU pool sizing and autoscaler policies. This is a planning artifact for infra & capacity owners to shape reservations, prewarm windows, and fallback rules.

Executive summary:
- Goal: Size regional pools so that we have at least 1.5x the 99th-percentile tokens/sec demand available without violating SLOs for 99th-p99 latency on generation endpoints.
- Time horizon: Jan–Mar 2028 (planning -> procurement/commitment decisions due by 2027-12-15).
- Key outcome: recommended GPU allocations by region, per-model routing tiers, and three burst buckets (steady, surge, flash) with associated prewarm and cooldown settings.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Mix: 55% decode tokens (generation), 35% prefill/prompt tokens, 10% embeddings/other control calls by token count.
- Average tokens per request: 300 tokens for chat-generation endpoints; 20 tokens for embedding calls.
- Model mix weighted toward medium/large open models (approx 65% of load on H100-optimized variants, 25% on A100, 10% on quantized L4 variants for low-cost routes).
- KV cache hit-rate assumed 18% during peak for chat workloads (improves effective throughput).
- Prefill-heavy workflows (long-context) increase per-request GPU hours — accounted as 1.35x decode cost multiplier for these requests.

Regional peak projections (peak tokens/sec, peak QPS equivalent):
- us-west1:
  - projected peak tokens/sec (99p): 320,000
  - projected peak QPS (99p; 300 avg tokens/request): ~1,067 QPS
- us-east4:
  - projected peak tokens/sec (99p): 400,000
  - projected peak QPS: ~1,333 QPS
- europe-west1:
  - projected peak tokens/sec (99p): 210,000
  - projected peak QPS: ~700 QPS
- asia-southeast1:
  - projected peak tokens/sec (99p): 140,000
  - projected peak QPS: ~467 QPS
- global-embeddings-burst (cross-region): 60,000 tokens/sec (avg 20 tokens/request -> 3,000 QPS)

Headroom targets and safety margins (sentinel policy):
- Baseline headroom target: provision capacity = 1.5x 99p tokens/sec for each region (this yields ~33% spare capacity after peak consumption).
- Surge bucket: allow additional short-term burst up to 2.0x 99p for periods <= 10 minutes; must be covered by prewarms and burst credits (see policy below).
- Flash bucket: ephemeral allowance up to 3.0x 99p for <= 60 seconds using fallback lanes (smaller models, degraded latency SLOs allowed, partial responses), logging gated.
- Utilization SLO: overall pool target utilization should be maintained between 48–62% over rolling 1h at peak windows to preserve fast cold-start headroom and to reduce tail latency risk.

GPU pool recommendations (by region):
- us-west1 (recommended mix): 24 H100-80GB, 8 A100-80GB, 18 L4 (quantized lanes) -> rationale: H100 handles highest-throughput and long-context variants; L4 for low-cost embedding-heavy routes and flash lanes.
- us-east4: 30 H100-80GB, 10 A100-80GB, 10 L4 -> highest user base and expected peak.
- europe-west1: 16 H100-80GB, 6 A100-80GB, 8 L4.
- asia-southeast1: 10 H100-80GB, 4 A100-80GB, 6 L4.
Notes: these allocations assume effective token/sec per H100 = 11k tokens/sec (median, mixed models), A100 = 7k tokens/sec, L4 = 1.2k tokens/sec for quantized emb/gen routes. Apply KV cache hit-rate multiplier (1.18) to effective throughput.

Scaling & routing policies (practical rules):
- Primary routing: prefer lowest-latency region with sufficient capacity, fall back by cost tier (H100 -> A100 -> L4).
- Canary rule: new model versions start in canary lanes with a hard cap of 5% of pool QPS; promotion only after quality checks and warm-up.
- Autoscaler behavior for peak windows:
  - Scale-up threshold: when 1m rolling tokens/sec >= 85% of provisioned capacity for 3 consecutive minutes, trigger scale-up increment of 10% of pool size (bounded by max burst addition).
  - Prewarm behavior: for scheduled events (marketing releases, partner launches) define prewarm window 30–120 minutes depending on expected multiplier; for surprise surges rely on burst credit and flash lanes.
  - Cooldown: after sustained drop to <=60% of provisioned capacity for 15 minutes, downscale in 5% steps with 20-minute cool-down between steps.

Burst credit accounting and cost control:
- Maintain a global burst-credit bank per region equivalent to 8 hours of steady-state average consumption (used only for surge events).
- Chargeback model: temporary burst pulls billed to product team budgets with rate multiplier (2.5x per-token cost) to incentivize pre-scheduling for predictable events.

Fallback and graceful degradation strategies:
- Tiered model fallback: route to smaller quantized variant (L4) with lower token-per-second cost but higher latency; if still saturated, return partial response + retry token to client with guidance to retry.
- Response shaping: for flash buckets enforce response truncation and shorter decode windows to keep token amplification low.

Monitoring signals to watch (alerts + dashboards):
- tokens/sec (1m/5m/1h) per region and per model-class.
- pool utilization (GPU vCPU equivalent), active context sizes, average tokens per request.
- prefill vs decode token ratios changing >10% week-over-week.
- KV cache hit-rate and its impact on effective throughput.
- ramp failure rate: scale-up attempts that fail due to insufficient quota/hot-spotting.

Open risks and unknowns:
- Model architecture changes (stateful context growth) could increase per-request GPU time beyond the 1.35x multiplier used — sensitivity analysis recommended.
- Cloud provider SKU deprecation or supply constraints for H100 in specific regions (asia) could force heavier reliance on A100 or remote routing.
- Unplanned viral events: current sentinel policy caps flash at 60s; sustained viral events longer than 30 minutes will require emergency reserve/pool borrowing across regions.

Action items (owners & dates):
- [Maya Chen] finalize procurement ask and submit reserved capacity request for us-east4 H100s by 2027-12-15.
- [Arjun Patel] add per-model throughput tests that account for long-context prefill flows by 2026-12-08 (JIRA-INFRA-1123).
- [Sofia Ramirez] implement burst-credit accounting in billing pipeline and expose spend dashboard by 2027-01-10.
- [Liam O'Connor] add sentinel alerts for KV hit-rate drop below 12% by 2026-12-05.

Appendix — sensitivity quick checks (for execs):
- If average tokens/request increases from 300 -> 450, regional H100 need increases ~1.35x; reserve procurement should reflect the higher baseline.
- If KV cache hit-rate improves to 30%, effective capacity increases ~12% across pools — can reduce spot L4 counts but keep H100/commit levels intact.

Notes & context links: refer to linked artifacts for the model-benchmark sheet and recent runtime PRs. This is a working doc — expect revisions after model-benchmarking and prefill stress tests finish.
